newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Former Alcatel chief's sentence suspended.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Former Alcatel chief's sentence suspended.

text.p: The former chairman of French industrial giant Alcatel Alsthom received a three-year suspended jail sentence and a fine on Tuesday for plundering company funds to pay for security work on his private homes.

Pierre Suard, forced to resign in June 1995 after being placed under judicial investigation, was convicted by a district court in the Paris suburb of Evry of abusing corporate funds and fined two million francs ($345,000).

But the court rejected a prosecution call to send him to prison for six months, and a representative of Alcatel's trade unions, who were civil plaintiffs in the case, complained that the bosses had escaped with light sentences.

Suard, 62, reported to have been France's highest paid chief executive, was also ordered to repay 4.9 million francs ($845,000) to Alcatel Alsthom, the cost of extensive security systems installed in his three homes.

The man who led the electronics and telecommunications equipment manufacturer through privatisation in 1987, making it France's second biggest industrial group and a world player, had no comment on leaving court but his lawyer said he would appeal.

"This condemnation is unjust, we dispute the very principle and we are immediately going to submit an appeal to prove that every word of what we contend is exact," defence counsel Maurice Guigui told reporters.
Suard had told the court he had taken the security measures on the advice of the government after the head of carmaker Renault was assassinated by hard-left urban guerrillas in 1986.
The verdict came in the midst of a parliamentary election campaign in which the issue of sleaze involving politicians and business executives has played a role.
Pierre Guichet, former chairman of the Alcatel CIT telecommunications subsidiary, was acquitted of abuse of corporate funds but fined 100,000 francs ($17,200) for forgery.
Some 40 other executives were convicted in the case.

The two Alcatel CIT managers who revealed the affair in 1993 after being fired, Jose Corral and Antonio Leal, received the harshest sentences, illustrating that there is no reward for whistle-blowing in France.
Leal was jailed for three years and fined two million francs ($345,000). Corral was given six months in prison with another 18 months suspended and fined 300,000 francs ($52,000).
A building contractor, Marc Dacheville, was also given a three-year prison sentence and fined one million francs ($172,000).

Suard, a trained engineer, won little public sympathy when he went on television in 1995 looking ill at ease and told viewers of the tears the case had caused his elderly relatives -- modest country people who could not understand it.

He is still under investigation in a separate case involving alleged overcharging of state telecommunications utility France Telecom by Alcatel, which led to an investigating magistrate's order barring him from contact with other company executives and effectively forcing him to resign.
The Supreme Court is due to rule on May 27 on a motion by Suard to have that case dismissed.
Suard was so angered by the charges of overbilling by a former Alcatel employee that he acknowledged having paid $6,000 out of his own pocket to have a private sleuth tail the whistle-blower.
